turns.prompt_text: can I print in B5 format from my MFC-L2820DW?
turns.response_html:
Yes, you can print in B5 format with your Brother MFC-L2820DW.

The printer supports both B5 (JIS) and B5 (ISO) standards directly from the standard paper tray. This is a great size for things like personal journals, specialized brochures, or even some of those technical manuals you've been picking up lately.

How to Set it Up

To ensure the printer handles the B5 paper correctly, you’ll need to adjust both the physical tray and the software settings:

  1. Adjust the Paper Tray:
    • Open the paper tray and slide the paper guides to the B5 markings.
    • Place your B5 paper in the tray, ensuring it sits flat and is not overfilled.
  2. Update the Printer Settings:
    • On the printer’s touchscreen, go to Settings > All Settings > General Setup > Tray Setting.
    • Select Paper Size and choose B5.
  3. Adjust the Computer Driver:
    • When you're ready to print from your Mac or PC, open the Print dialog.
    • Go to Properties or Preferences (on Windows) or Paper Size (on macOS) and select B5 to match the tray setting.

Key Considerations

  • Manual Feed Slot: If you only have a single sheet of B5 paper or a heavier cardstock, you can use the manual feed slot on the front. This slot supports widths from 3" to 8.5" and lengths from 5" to 14", which easily accommodates B5 (6.9" x 9.8").
  • Duplex Printing: Note that while the printer supports automatic double-sided printing for Letter and A4 sizes, it generally does not support automatic duplexing for B5. You may need to flip the pages manually if you want to print on both sides.

turns.prompt_text: On mac, the B5 does not show up
turns.response_html:
It’s a common quirk with Brother printers on macOS: Brother doesn't actually provide a dedicated "CUPS" driver for the MFC-L2820DW on recent versions of macOS. Instead, it relies entirely on AirPrint, which sometimes hides certain standard sizes like B5.

Since the printer hardware itself supports B5, you can manually "unlock" it by creating a custom paper size in your print dialog.

How to add B5 to your Mac Print Dialog

  1. Open any document (like a PDF or a Word file) and go to File > Print (or press Cmd + P).
  2. In the Print window, look for the Paper Size dropdown menu.
  3. Scroll to the very bottom and select Manage Custom Sizes....
  4. Click the plus (+) sign to create a new entry.
  5. Double-click the name "Untitled" and rename it B5 (JIS) or B5 (ISO).
  6. Enter the following dimensions (depending on which B5 paper you have):
    • B5 (JIS): Width: 182 mm | Height: 257 mm
    • B5 (ISO): Width: 176 mm | Height: 250 mm
    • Note: If your Mac is set to inches, JIS is 7.17" x 10.12" and ISO is 6.93" x 9.84".
  7. Set the Non-Printable Area to "User Defined" and put 0.16 inches (4mm) for all sides to be safe.
  8. Click OK.

Making it "Stick"

Once you’ve created this, B5 will now appear in your Paper Size list for all future print jobs.

Pro-tip: Since you enjoy terminal customization, you can actually see all your printer's supported PPD (PostScript Printer Description) features by running lpoptions -l in your Fish shell. If B5 is truly missing from the driver's internal list, creating the custom size as described above is the cleanest way to bypass the AirPrint limitation.

turns.prompt_text: I've added the B5, but it still does not show up on the Brother IPrint&Scan app
turns.response_html:
The reason B5 isn't showing up in Brother iPrint&Scan—even after you added it to macOS—is that iPrint&Scan is a "sandboxed" app. It doesn't look at your Mac's custom system paper sizes; it only displays the hard-coded sizes that the printer reports via its internal firmware.

Since your MFC-L2820DW does support B5, but the app is being stubborn, here are the two ways to fix this:

1. The "Web Management" Fix (Highest Success)

The app often checks the printer's current tray configuration. If the printer thinks it's holding "Letter," the app might filter out B5 to prevent a "size mismatch" error.

  1. Find your printer's IP Address (you can find this in your Fish shell using arp -a or on the printer's LCD under Network > WLAN > TCP/IP).
  2. Type that IP address into your web browser to open the Web Based Management page.
  3. Go to the Print tab (or General Setup) and look for Tray Setting.
  4. Change the Paper Size for the tray from "Letter" to B5.
  5. Click Submit.
  6. Restart iPrint&Scan on your Mac. It should now see B5 as the active, supported size.

2. Bypass iPrint&Scan Entirely (The Pro Move)

Since you are a software engineer and likely comfortable with the standard macOS interface, you’ll find that iPrint&Scan is actually more restrictive than the native macOS print system.

Instead of using the app:

  1. Open your document in Preview or your IDE.
  2. Press Cmd + P.
  3. Select your Brother printer.
  4. Your custom B5 size will be available here, and macOS will send the raw data to the printer. Because you've already set the physical guides in the tray, it will print perfectly.

Troubleshooting the "Missing" Size

If it still won't show up in any app, it's likely because your Mac added the printer using the AirPrint driver by default, which is "lite" and often ignores custom sizes.

To fix this, you can force macOS to use a more robust driver:

  1. Go to System Settings > Printers & Scanners.
  2. Delete your current printer (click it, then click Remove Printer).
  3. Click Add Printer....
  4. Select your MFC-L2820DW, but in the Use dropdown at the bottom, don't leave it on "Auto/AirPrint."
  5. Select Generic PostScript Printer (or if "Brother CUPS" appears, choose that).

This "Standard" driver is much more receptive to those custom dimensions you programmed in earlier.
